text.p: Italian debt markets were down but not unduly depressed in late European trade, with much activity between the December and March futures contracts on LIFFE.

Traders said volumes had been reasonable due to spread activity between the front month, which expires next week, and the March contract. One trader noted the spread between the two had closed in from 99 to 86 basis points and he speculated this might mean people were wanting to be long the March contract.
The December LIFFE contract was 13 basis points down at 127.87 while the March future was eight off at 126.98. The July 2006 Btp was 25 basis points down at 108.54.
The lira strengthened slightly in late European trade to 990.00/0.50 from a low of 996.50 earlier.
At home, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said consumer price inflation would continue to register "very slight" falls and ruled out a reversal of the downward trend of recent months.

Parties in the centre-left government said they were ready to change a controversial "Euro-tax" plan in the 1997 budget with proposed amendments to reduce the burden on self-employed Italians to be published on later on Wednesday.
The changes are expected to be achieved without lowering the total amount of revenue expected from the tax.
Italian Renewal, the centrist party led by Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini, unveiled alternative tax measures to those in the "Euro-tax".

It suggested scrapping a tax on severance pay intended to raise 3.5 trillion lire, raising one trillion via a corporate tax and the remaining 2.5 trillion lire from more revenue efforts and a one-off charge on early-retirement pensions for people under the age of 50 to 52.
